observation_summary: The CSVPrinter incorrectly escapes the nullString value (e.g., '\N' becomes '\\N') when it should be written as a literal. This is a procedural error in the printing logic where the nullString is treated as a standard field value subject to escaping/quoting rules.
hypothesis: The CSVPrinter class is incorrectly applying escaping logic to the nullString value. When a field is null, the printer should output the configured nullString literal directly without passing it through the escaping or quoting mechanisms that are intended for regular data fields.
prediction: I expect to find that the CSVPrinter.print method (or the method responsible for printing individual fields) does not have a special case to bypass escaping/quoting when the value is null and a nullString is defined.
experiment_rationale: The failure is clearly in the output generation logic of the CSVPrinter. The test cases show that the printer is applying transformations (escaping) to the nullString that are inappropriate for the MySQL format requirements. This is a local procedural error in how the printer handles null values.
reasoning_summary: The bug report and test failures confirm that the CSVPrinter is applying escaping to the nullString. The fix requires modifying the printing logic to treat the nullString as a literal when a null value is encountered, which is a classic algorithmic/method-level correction.
